articles.title: Anthropic's IPO filing shows soaring revenue, mounting costs, and "existential" risks
articles.summary: Anthropic warns in its own IPO prospectus that its AI technology could pose "existential risks to humanity." Revenue grew twelvefold in 2025 to $4.6 billion, but the operating loss widened to $8.06 billion. Backers are aiming for a valuation above $2 trillion, and the IPO is expected to set the bar for the entire AI industry. articles.title: Goldman Sachs expects Big Tech to spend $1.2 trillion on AI infrastructure by 2027, dwarfing Wall Street estimates
articles.summary: Goldman Sachs projects that Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Oracle, and Meta will pour a combined $1.2 trillion into AI infrastructure in 2027, more than 50 percent above this year's levels. Measured against GDP, it would be the biggest investment cycle since railroad construction in the 19th century. Bottlenecks in power, labor, and memory chips could slow the pace, though. articles.title: I built a generic multi-step flow engine on top of Laravel controllers
articles.summary: At Zeney Pay we build a mobile app for cross-border money transfers and real-time currency conversion. A fintech backend is mostly flows: sign-in with 2FA, registration, KYC, "forgot my PIN", setting up a transaction PIN, sending money. None of them fit in a single HTTP request. For a while we handled them the way most teams do, and it went badly. This post covers what went wrong, how we changed our thinking, the design decisions behind the result, and the package that came out of it: na2axl/laravel-api-flow. How it went wrong Our flows were spread out in two ways: On the backend, one flow was split across several controllers. AuthController@login, OtpController@verify, PinController@check... Each endpoint had to work out for itself whether the caller had actually gone through the earlier steps. On the frontend, the mobile app held the rest. It decided which screen came next, when to skip the OTP screen, and what "back" meant. This gave us several sources of truth for the same business
